doc.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

chapter: Arriving in New York and Mingus
title: The Five Spot and Mingus's band
summary: Pause for water, then he describes hanging at the Five Spot where Mingus's quintet played, and Red Callender's absence from the Birdland run.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well I think you’ve informed a lot of people along the way. Do you recall the first time you met Charles Mingus?
Oh yes. Who can forget a thing like that? Can I be heard at all?
Okay. It seems like my voice is fading as we speak.
Feel free to take some water. We can pause, there’s no problem with that at all.
We were talking about Charles Mingus.

Yeah. I used to go down to the Five Spot. The guys in there knew me and they didn’t like dislike me or anything, the guys who owned the place, they were very tolerant of young musicians who wanted to hang and listen. And Mingus was there with a quintet with Charles McPherson, Lonnie Hillyer, Danny Richmond, and Jaki Byard. So I had met Jaki because I lived in — I had an apartment in Boston when I was in the Navy. And I met Jaki through Tony Williams, whose mother I rented the room from. So I’d already started playing the tuba, I’d been playing for about a year in New York. And I went to see Mingus. I didn’t have any money. I would have liked to have spent some money but I just didn’t have any. And they were kind of looking at me like oh this guy’s hanging out again. So I was trying to sit in the back and be small so the Termini brothers wouldn’t look at me so much. And Mingus had just finished his “Mingus at Monterey” recording, a big band with L.A. cats in it and his quintet. And he hired Red Callender to come and play the tuba on that date. So it was a great record, and when he came back to New York he wanted to play that music, that Monterey music, at Birdland, the old Birdland, with Pee Wee and everything — Pee Wee Marquette.

And Mingus had — this night I came in the Five Spot — Mingus had just gotten the word that Red Callender wouldn’t come east. He had contractual obligations and they wouldn’t let him out to come —a whole week. So he had to call Mingus to tell him that that night. Mingus was not happy. Red Callender was his first bass teacher, I don’t know, people don’t realize that.
I did not. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
